text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Foreign Minister Amr Moussa said Egypt wanted an appropriate and acceptable timeframe for peace negotiations. He told al-Ahram in London that the European Union summit statement represents a basis for balanced action to save peace. An Arab common market is the foundation of the Middle East market in its proper sense, he added.

- Prime Minister Kamal Ganzouri will chair a meeting of seven ministers and the governor of the New Valley today to discuss investment projects in East Oweinat. Ganzouri will explain the government's concept of development in the region and the extent to which the private sector can contribute.
- Amr Moussa said Egypt would continue to play its role in salvaging the peace process and putting it back on the right track. He said the European role was very important.

- In its next meeting the cabinet will discuss a report on Toshka. The report says that work has started on reclaiming 140,000 acres (57,000 hectares) of land around the Aswan-Abu Simbel road. Eleven km (seven miles) of the main irrigation canal to Toshka has been dug at a cost of 128 million pounds ($38 million).
- The public prosecutor in Alexandria referred 20 people to the courts in connection with the leaking of second school certificate examination papers.
- Pensions will go up 10 percent from July 10.
- Amr Moussa and presidential adviser Osama el-Baz will visit Jordan tomorrow on a working visit to discuss developments in the peace process.
- An official source said that in the next few weeks practical steps will be taken to restore diplomatic relations between Kuwait on one side and Jordan and Yemen on the other.

- The Sheikh of al-Azhar, Mohamed Sayyed Tantawi, called for a meeting of Moslem, Christian and Jewish leaders to decide the status of Jerusalem. For the first time he favoured joint administration by the three religions.
